title: Infinite Request Retry Queue (Queue Accumulation)
pattern: Storing failed requests or background jobs in an unbounded queue/collection for later retrying, without enforcing an upper bound on queue size or dropping old/stale requests.
why_bad: When an downstream dependency suffers a prolonged outage, a retry queue that has no maximum size will grow indefinitely [133, 134]. This results in massive memory footprint growth and eventually causes OOM panics [133, 216]. Furthermore, upon recovery, the server must process hours of stale backlog (often email or messages that are no longer wanted), causing cascading failures and prolonged recovery times [133, 134].
detection: Identify queues or vectors designated for retrying failed operations that lack a capped maximum capacity or an aging/TTL eviction mechanism.
fix: Enforce a strict maximum capacity on the retry queue, dropping or rejecting requests (e.g., LIFO/FIFO eviction) once the queue is full [134, 216].
source: Marianne Bellotti, *Kill It with Fire*, Chapter 9 / passages [133, 134]; Michael T. Nygard, *Release It!*, Chapter 10 (Steady State) / passage [216].
